subject.title: feat(cron): stream schedule sources with durable source identity

question: Should OpenClaw accept the Track D stream-source schedule as a core cron capability under the existing `cron.triggers.enabled` trust boundary, rather than defer it to the broader automation-unification program or an extension seam?
rationale: This PR introduces a new long-lived process and persisted schedule model across core gateway, protocol, agent-tool, CLI, and UI surfaces; code review alone cannot determine whether that product and authorization boundary is the intended permanent direction.

options.title: Sponsor the core stream schedule
options.body: Accept stream schedules as the next automation-unification deliverable after confirming upgrade safety and live lifecycle proof.

options.title: Defer to the umbrella program
options.body: Pause this PR until the open automation-unification issue establishes the final core ownership and rollout sequence.

options.title: Require an extension seam first
options.body: Keep core generic and define the missing plugin or gateway extension contract before accepting a bundled process-stream implementation.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core stream schedule
recommendation.body: Accept stream schedules as the next automation-unification deliverable after confirming upgrade safety and live lifecycle proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor authored the umbrella automation-unification proposal and the stream-schedule implementation history supplied with this review.
